title: Tagliata di manzo
subtitle: Sliced grilled steak with rocket and Parmesan
excerpt: Tagliata di manzo is a Florentine way of serving steak: the beef is grilled hot and fast, rested, then sliced thinly and laid over a mound of dressed rocket with shaved Parmesan. It is a restaurant staple across Italy and one of the simplest beef dishes to get right at home.
sourceNotes: Tuscan regional recipe. Tagliata is a Florentine way of serving beef, popularised alongside the bistecca alla fiorentina tradition of thick-cut grilled steaks. Method drawn from traditional Tuscan sources and Anna Del Conte, Gastronomy of Italy (2001).

glossaryTerms.definition: Italian for 'sliced'; in cooking, tagliata di manzo refers to grilled beef that is rested and then cut across the grain into thin slices, served at medium-rare.

content.text: Tagliata di manzo is sliced grilled steak served over rocket with Parmesan shavings and a drizzle of olive oil. The

method means the steak is cooked in one large piece, rested, then sliced against the grain. Ribeye or sirloin works best: enough fat to stay juicy at medium-rare. The rocket should be dressed simply with lemon and oil before the steak goes on top.

items.prepNote: or sirloin, about 3 cm thick, at room temperature
juice of half, wedges to serve
for seasoning the steak and the rocket

content.text: Pat {{beef-ribeye}} of steak dry and season generously with salt and pepper. Heat a griddle pan or heavy frying pan over the highest heat until smoking. Cook the steak for 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium-rare (about 55°C at the centre). Rest on a board for 5 minutes.
While the steak rests, dress {{rocket}} of rocket with 2 tablespoons of olive oil and a squeeze of lemon. Season lightly. Spread over a large serving plate.

Slice the steak thinly across the grain. Lay the slices over the rocket. Drizzle with the remaining {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} of olive oil, scatter over the shaved {{parmesan}} of Parmesan, and add sea salt flakes. Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

items.cause: Not rested long enough or sliced with the grain rather than across it.
items.fix: Rest for a full 5 minutes. Always slice across the grain, perpendicular to the muscle fibres.

items.cause: Pan not hot enough, or too thick for the timing given.
items.fix: The pan must be properly hot before the steak goes on. A 3 cm steak takes 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium-rare; adjust by 1 minute each way for thicker or thinner cuts.

content.text: Tagliata is rooted in Tuscan beef cooking, where the Chianina breed has long been prized for its lean, flavourful meat. In Tuscany, bistecca alla fiorentina is the grand occasion dish; tagliata is what you make on a summer evening when you want beef quickly. The rocket and Parmesan balance the richness and make the plate feel lighter than it is.
